title: Capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation through TRPV1–SSR4 interaction
title_zh: 辣椒素通过TRPV1–SSR4相互作用抑制小胶质细胞炎症
abstract: Abstract Background Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of microglial response during neuroinflammation, a key pathological feature of various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Capsaicin, the primary pungent component in chili peppers, executes its anti-inflammatory properties as a TRPV1 agonist. Although the mechanism of TRPV1 channel activation and signal transduction by capsaicin has been extensively studied, the protein–protein interaction-based mechanisms by which TRPV1 modulates microglial inflammatory responses in the context of neurodegeneration remains unclear. Methods We used a lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation model to examine the effects of TRPV1 activation and pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating on microglial inflammatory responses. Proximity labeling-based proteomics, bioluminescence resonance energy transfer, and NanoLuc Binary Technology were used to identify and characterize TRPV1-interacting proteins. Signal sequence receptor subunit 4 (SSR4) knockdown and forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 were performed to assess the functional contribution of the TRPV1–SSR4 interaction. Structural modeling, BRET-based domain mapping, and colocalization analyses were further used to examine the molecular and subcellular features of SSR4 recruitment by TRPV1. Results In the neuroinflammatory model, the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin attenuated pro-inflammatory cytokine production, neuronal apoptosis, microgliosis, and microglial soma enlargement in a TRPV1-dependent manner. Notably, pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating by capsazepine did not abolish the anti-inflammatory action of capsaicin, suggesting an alternative mechanism of action beyond the canonical ligand-gated Ca 2 ⁺ influx. Screening of TRPV1 prey proteins and validation strategy identified SSR4 as a capsaicin-responsive, TRPV1-associated protein. SSR4 knockdown in microglia significantly diminished the suppression of inflammatory responses caused by TRPV1 activation. Conversely, forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 partially mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of TRPV1 activation. Further structural and cellular analyses suggested that the transmembrane region of TRPV1 supports SSR4 recruitment. Conclusions Our findings suggest that capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation mediated by the TRPV1–SSR4 interaction, providing new insights into the chemical biology basis of TRPV1 interoceptive signaling and potential applications of natural TRPV1 agonists for modifying therapy of neuroinflammation-associated neurodegeneration.
abstract_zh: 背景：瞬时受体电位香草醛1（TRPV1）在神经炎症期间被越来越多地认定为小胶质细胞反应的重要调节因子，神经炎症是阿尔茨海默病等多种神经退行性疾病的关键病理特征。辣椒素是辣椒中主要的辛辣成分，作为TRPV1激动剂发挥其抗炎作用。虽然辣椒素激活TRPV1通道及信号转导机制已被广泛研究，但TRPV1通过蛋白‑蛋白相互作用调节小胶质细胞炎症反应的机制在神经退行性疾病背景下仍不清楚。方法：我们采用脂多糖诱导的急性神经炎症模型，研究TRPV1激活及TRPV1通道门控的药理阻断对小胶质细胞炎症反应的影响。通过邻近标记蛋白质组学、生物发光共振能量转移（BRET）和NanoLuc二元技术识别并表征TRPV1相互作用蛋白。对SSR4进行敲低并强制诱导TRPV1与SSR4相互作用，以评估TRPV1–SSR4相互作用的功能贡献。进一步利用结构建模、BRET域映射和共定位分析探讨SSR4被TRPV1招募的分子与亚细胞特征。结果：在神经炎症模型中，TRPV1激动剂辣椒素以TRPV1依赖方式抑制促炎细胞因子产生、神经元凋亡、小胶质细胞增生和小胶质细胞体积增大。值得注意的是，使用capsazepine药理阻断TRPV1通道门控并未消除辣椒素的抗炎作用，提示存在超出经典配体门控Ca²⁺流入的替代机制。筛选TRPV1捕获蛋白并验证策略发现SSR4为辣椒素响应的TRPV1相关蛋白。SSR4在小胶质细胞中的敲低显著削弱TRPV1激活所致炎症抑制。相反，强制诱导TRPV1与SSR4相互作用部分模拟了TRPV1激活的抗炎效应。进一步的结构与细胞分析表明TRPV1的跨膜区支持SSR4的招募。结论：我们的研究表明，辣椒素通过TRPV1–SSR4相互作用抑制小胶质细胞炎症，为TRPV1内感信号的化学生物学基础提供新见解，并提示天然TRPV1激动剂在调节神经炎症相关神经退行性疾病治疗中的潜在应用。
